frontend.lead: For frontend, Claude Code shines when it knows your framework, sees type errors and can look at the page just like you do.

steps.t: Tell it your stack in CLAUDE.md
steps.d: Run `/init` and add the framework and its version, the commands (`dev`, `build`, `test`) and how you handle styles and components. It reads this at the start of every session.
With `typescript-lsp`, Claude sees type errors after every edit and fixes them before you find them.
Context7 brings the docs for the exact version of your library, so it doesn't use old React, Next or Tailwind APIs.

steps.t: Show it how it should look
steps.d: Paste a screenshot with `Ctrl+V` or connect Figma. A marked-up image explains more than three paragraphs.

steps.t: Let it test in the browser
steps.d: With `claude --chrome` it opens the page, clicks around and reads the console; `/verify` builds and watches the app. Check it yourself too, on desktop and on mobile.

quiz.q: What is a language server plugin like `typescript-lsp` for?
o: Claude sees type errors after every edit
quiz.why: The language server gives Claude the same errors you see in your editor, right after it edits.

quiz.q: Claude uses an old API from your framework. What helps?
o: Context7, which brings the docs for the version you use
quiz.why: The model learned from earlier versions; Context7 gives it the current docs.

quiz.q: How do you show Claude how a screen should look?
o: With a screenshot (`Ctrl+V`) or the Figma design
You can't: it only understands text
quiz.why: Claude reads images: a screenshot or the original design saves back-and-forth.

quiz.q: What goes in a frontend project's CLAUDE.md?
o: The framework, the commands and the styling conventions
quiz.why: CLAUDE.md holds what Claude always needs to know about the project, never secrets.

quiz.q: What does `claude --chrome` do?
o: Connects Claude to Chrome to browse the page, click and read the console
quiz.why: That way Claude checks the result in a real browser instead of assuming it.

quiz.q: Before calling a visual change done, you should…
o: Look at it in the browser on desktop and on mobile
Ask it to make it prettier
quiz.why: Compiling says nothing about how it looks: check it at real widths.

backend.lead: In backend work, what matters is that Claude understands the code before touching it, tests what it changes and doesn't open security holes.

steps.d: With `/init` and by hand: how to start the database, run migrations and tests, and which folders are off limits. Without it, Claude guesses.
In plan mode Claude explores the code and proposes the steps without editing anything. You correct it there, while it's cheap.
Ask for a test that reproduces the bug and fails, then the fix. That way you know it really fixed it.
`/security-review` looks for vulnerabilities in your branch's changes: injections, exposed data, weak permissions.
With the Sentry plugin, Claude reads production errors and stack traces to investigate them without you copying anything.

quiz.q: What is plan mode for in a big backend change?
o: Claude explores and proposes the steps before editing
quiz.why: Fixing a plan costs far less than undoing twenty edited files.

quiz.q: What does `/security-review` do?
o: Looks for vulnerabilities in your branch's changes
quiz.why: It reviews the diff with a focus on security before it reaches production.

quiz.q: To fix a bug, you should ask for…
o: First a test that reproduces it, then the fix
A rewrite of the whole module
quiz.why: The failing test proves the bug and, once it passes, proves the fix.

quiz.q: What does the Sentry plugin give it?
o: Reading real production errors with their stack traces
quiz.why: It investigates with real data instead of guessing what happened.

quiz.q: What should go in a backend's CLAUDE.md?
o: How to start the database, migrate and run the tests
quiz.why: Commands and rules yes; secrets never.

quiz.q: What is an MCP server?
o: A connection that gives Claude external tools, like your database or your tickets
quiz.why: MCP connects Claude to other systems; the Supabase one, for example, lets it query your database.

fullstack.lead: Fullstack means running the whole loop: plan, code, see it working, review and open the PR. Claude Code has a piece for each part.

steps.d: `/plan` plus the request: Claude goes through front and back and proposes the steps. You adjust them before it touches anything.

steps.t: Let it run and test it
steps.d: `/run` starts the app to see the change working and `/verify` checks it does what it should, not just that the tests are green.
The `commit-commands` plugin commits, pushes and opens the PR; with `/install-github-app` you can mention @claude in issues and PRs.
`claude --worktree` opens a separate copy of the repo on another branch: one session fixes a bug while another builds a feature.
`/diff` shows what changed and `/code-review` looks for bugs in the diff with several agents.

quiz.q: What is `claude --worktree` for?
o: Working on another branch in a separate copy without stepping on your work
quiz.why: Each worktree is its own folder: two sessions don't overwrite each other's files.

quiz.q: What does `/run` do?
o: Starts the app to see the change working
quiz.why: Seeing the app running catches problems tests don't.

quiz.q: What's a good order for a new feature?
quiz.why: Each stage catches mistakes while they're still cheap to fix.

quiz.q: What is `/install-github-app` for?
o: Mentioning @claude in GitHub issues and PRs
quiz.why: It installs the Claude app on your repo and it replies where you mention it.

quiz.q: What does `/diff` show?
o: The changes it made to the files
quiz.why: Reviewing the diff is the fastest way to know what it touched.

quiz.q: You finished a task and are starting a different one. What do you do?
o: `/clear` to start with a clean context
quiz.why: Old context confuses it and spends tokens on every message.

mobile.lead: In mobile, Claude doesn't touch your phone, but it does understand the compiler, the simulator and your backend if you introduce them.

steps.t: Tell it how to run the app
steps.d: In CLAUDE.md: platform (iOS, Android or both), whether you use Expo or native, and the commands to run in the simulator and build.
`swift-lsp` and `kotlin-lsp` show Claude the compiler errors after every edit.
The official Expo plugin brings skills to create, debug and ship React Native apps.
If a screen looks wrong, paste the screenshot with `Ctrl+V` and tell it what you expected to see.
With the Firebase plugin it handles the database, auth and functions without leaving the terminal.

quiz.q: What do you get from `swift-lsp` or `kotlin-lsp`?
o: Claude sees compiler errors after every edit
It publishes itself to the store
quiz.why: It fixes build errors right away, without you copying them.

quiz.q: A screen looks wrong in the simulator. What do you give Claude?
o: A screenshot with `Ctrl+V` and what you expected
quiz.why: The screenshot and the expectation tell it exactly what to fix.

quiz.q: What should go in a mobile app's CLAUDE.md?
o: The platform and the commands to run and build it
quiz.why: Without the commands it can't build or test; signing keys never go there.

quiz.q: Which stack is the `expo` plugin for?
quiz.why: They're Expo's official skills for React Native.

quiz.q: Claude can't touch your phone. How do you verify a change?
o: Run the tests and try it yourself in the simulator or on the phone
quiz.why: What you see and tap has to be checked by a person on the device.

quiz.q: Why use plan mode before migrating a whole screen?
o: To review the steps before it edits many files
quiz.why: A big change is worth agreeing on before starting.

devops.lead: In DevOps, Claude Code is for automation: rules that always apply, tasks that run on their own and Claude inside your scripts.

steps.d: With `/hooks` you run a command on each event: format after editing or block an `rm -rf`. A hook never forgets; an instruction in CLAUDE.md sometimes does.
`/loop` repeats a request in your session; `/schedule` creates a routine in the cloud that runs even if you close the terminal.
`claude -p` runs without a UI and with `--output-format json` the script reads the answer without guessing.
There are official plugins for AWS, Cloudflare and Datadog: Claude reads logs and metrics, and operates the infrastructure.
`/sandbox` limits which files and network the commands can reach; `/permissions` defines what's allowed, what's asked and what's denied.

quiz.q: What's the difference between a hook and an instruction in CLAUDE.md?
o: The hook always runs; Claude can skip the instruction
Hooks only work in the cloud
quiz.why: Claude Code runs the hook, not the model: it doesn't depend on remembering.

quiz.q: What is `claude -p` for?
o: Running Claude without a UI, in scripts or CI
quiz.why: It's the non-interactive mode: question, answer and exit.

quiz.q: What's the difference between `/loop` and `/schedule`?
o: `/loop` repeats in your session; `/schedule` runs in the cloud even if you close the terminal
quiz.why: For something that must happen every day even when you're away, use a routine with `/schedule`.

quiz.q: What does `/sandbox` do?
o: Limits which files and network the commands can reach
quiz.why: It isolates commands so a mistake stays where it belongs.

quiz.q: Why use `--output-format json` in CI?
o: So the script reads the result without parsing free text
quiz.why: A fixed format doesn't break when the wording changes.

quiz.q: You want to know if the deploy fails while you work on something else. What do you use?
o: A `/loop` that checks it every so often and tells you
quiz.why: The loop keeps watch for you in the same session.

data.lead: With data, Claude Code explores files, writes queries and charts, and does research. Your job is to check that the numbers add up.

steps.d: With `duckdb-skills` Claude reads CSV, Parquet or JSON and queries them with SQL without loading anything into a database.
Anthropic's `xlsx` and `pdf` skills open, edit and create spreadsheets with formulas, and pull tables out of PDFs.
`/dataviz` picks the chart form and validates the palette for color blindness and contrast.
`/deep-research` searches the web in parallel, cross-checks sources and writes a report with citations.
Ask for the query it used and compare it with a total you know. An unchecked number doesn't go in a report.

quiz.q: What does the `xlsx` skill do?
o: Opens, edits and creates Excel spreadsheets with formulas
quiz.why: It works on the file directly, with formulas and charts.

quiz.q: A number in the report looks odd. What do you do?
o: Ask for the query and check it against a known total
quiz.why: The query shows where the number came from; the known total, whether it adds up.

quiz.q: What is `/deep-research` for?
o: Researching the web and writing a report with cited sources
quiz.why: The citations let you check every fact.

quiz.q: What's wise before analyzing a big CSV?
o: Have Claude look at the schema and a sample before concluding
Paste the whole file into the chat
quiz.why: Understanding the columns and odd values avoids false conclusions.

quiz.q: What is `/dataviz`?
o: A built-in guide for clear charts and dashboards
quiz.why: It ships with Claude Code and checks the colors and form of the chart.

quiz.q: A dataset has personal data. What do you do before working on it with AI?
o: Anonymize it or use a sample without personal data
quiz.why: Personal data shouldn't leave where it lives unless it has to.

designer.lead: For design, Claude Code turns your screens into code, sketches layouts and pieces, and respects a visual system if you give it one.

steps.d: The Figma plugin reads your files, components and tokens, and turns them into code with the real measurements.
`/design` sketches screens, flows or landing pages on a Claude Design canvas.
The `theme-factory` skill applies color and type themes; `brand-guidelines` is the model for building your own brand's skill.
With the Canva plugin it creates, adapts and reviews designs without leaving the terminal.
With `claude --chrome` Claude opens the page; you check it on mobile and desktop before approving it.

quiz.q: What do you get by connecting Figma?
o: Claude reads the design and turns it into code with the real measurements
quiz.why: It works with the real components and tokens instead of copying them from a screenshot.

quiz.q: What is a design token?
o: A named value (color, spacing, font) reused across the whole design
quiz.why: Tokens make changing a color a matter of changing one value.

quiz.q: How do you explain a visual detail?
o: With a marked-up screenshot and what you want changed
quiz.why: The more concrete the reference, the less back-and-forth.

quiz.q: What does `/design` do?
o: Sketches screens, flows or landing pages on a canvas
quiz.why: It's a built-in skill for sketching in Claude Design.

quiz.q: What is the `brand-guidelines` skill for?
o: It's the model for building a skill with your brand's identity
quiz.why: It applies Anthropic's identity; copying it, you build yours.

quiz.q: Before approving a screen you should…
o: See it on mobile and on desktop
quiz.why: What looks good at 1440 px can break at 375 px.

video.lead: With video, Claude Code writes the video as code, runs ffmpeg for you and makes GIFs. The final eye is still yours.

steps.d: The Remotion skills teach Claude to build videos with code: text, animations and scenes that get rendered.
The HyperFrames plugin turns HTML into video, great for pieces with data or changing text.
The `slack-gif-creator` skill makes light animated GIFs for Slack or social media.
With `!` in front you run the command in the terminal and Claude sees the output: trim, scale or compress without looking up flags.

steps.t: Watch it all the way through
steps.d: Watch the full render before publishing: cuts, audio and text. Claude doesn't see the video the way you do.

quiz.q: What is Remotion?
o: A library for making videos with React and code
quiz.why: You describe the video in code and it renders: changing a text is editing one line.

quiz.q: What is the `!` at the start of a line for?
o: It runs that command in the terminal and Claude sees the output
quiz.why: It's bash mode: handy for ffmpeg and any command-line tool.

quiz.q: Who reviews the final video?
o: You, watching it all before publishing
Nobody: if it rendered, it's fine
quiz.why: Pacing, audio and fine details are judged by a person.

quiz.q: What's the advantage of making video with code?
o: Changing text, colors or length and rendering again
quiz.why: Versions and variants come out without manual editing.

quiz.q: You want to shrink a video without distorting it. What do you ask?
quiz.why: The `-2` computes the height to keep the aspect ratio.

quiz.q: Which music and photos can you use?
quiz.why: Copyright still applies even if an AI puts it together.

marketing.lead: For marketing, Claude Code isn't just for coding: it does research, writes in your brand's voice and builds documents and decks.

steps.d: The `brand-voice` plugin finds how your brand speaks, writes a guide and checks that every text follows it.
`/deep-research` searches the web, cross-checks sources and gives you a report with citations to back every fact.
The `docx` and `pptx` skills create Word and PowerPoint files; `/slides` builds a deck from your request.
With the Canva plugin it creates and adapts pieces for each network without redoing them.
Verify every fact and every promise at its source. What gets published is on you.

quiz.q: What is the `brand-voice` plugin for?
o: Making texts come out in your brand's tone
quiz.why: It builds the voice guide and checks that content follows it.

quiz.q: What do you give it for campaign copy?
o: Audience, goal, tone and an example you like
quiz.why: With concrete context the first draft is already useful.

quiz.q: Claude wrote a market statistic. What do you do?
o: Verify it at the source before publishing
Ask it to sound more confident
quiz.why: A false fact in a campaign is costly.

quiz.q: What does `/deep-research` return?
quiz.why: The citations let you check everything.

quiz.q: What does `/slides` do?
o: Builds a deck from your request
quiz.why: It creates the deck as a Claude Slides artifact.

quiz.q: Is Claude Code useful if you don't code?
o: Yes: it works with files, documents and tools, not just code
quiz.why: Many skills and plugins are for documents, research and design.

pm.lead: As a PM, Claude Code lets you read the code without programming, work tickets where they live and write specs and decks.

steps.d: With the Linear or Atlassian (Jira and Confluence) plugins, Claude reads and updates issues without copy and paste.
Open Claude in the repo and ask how something works. `/btw` asks a side question without adding it to the conversation.
The `doc-coauthoring` skill guides writing specs and proposals section by section.
The `product-management` plugin builds specs, roadmaps and syntheses of user interviews.
`/slides` turns your request into a deck ready to present.

quiz.q: What do you get by connecting Linear or Jira?
o: Claude reads and updates tickets without copy and paste
quiz.why: It works with the team's real information.

quiz.q: You want to understand how checkout works. What do you do?
o: Ask Claude in the repo where it is and how it works
quiz.why: Claude navigates the code and explains it in words.

quiz.q: What is `/btw`?
o: A side question that isn't added to the conversation
quiz.why: It's for a quick doubt without cluttering the context.

quiz.q: What does a good spec for Claude include?
o: Problem, users, acceptance criteria and what's out of scope
quiz.why: Acceptance criteria tell it when it's done.

quiz.q: What is `doc-coauthoring` for?
o: Writing specs and documents together, section by section
quiz.why: It's an Anthropic skill for collaborative documents.

quiz.q: What does the `product-management` plugin do?
o: Specs, roadmaps and user research syntheses
quiz.why: It's one of Anthropic's plugins by line of work.

qa.lead: In QA, Claude Code tests like a user, reproduces bugs with tests and reviews each change before it reaches production.

steps.d: The Playwright plugin automates the browser and builds end-to-end tests that walk through the app like a user.
Ask first for a test that fails with the bug. If it doesn't fail, the problem isn't understood yet.
`chrome-devtools-mcp` lets Claude read the page's console and network requests.
`/code-review` looks for bugs in the diff, a PR or a branch; the `pr-review-toolkit` plugin adds agents for tests and error handling.
`/verify` builds, runs and watches the app to check the change does what it should.

quiz.q: What does Playwright do?
o: Automates the browser to test flows like a user
quiz.why: It really walks through the app: clicks, forms and navigation.

quiz.q: What's wise before fixing a bug?
o: A test that reproduces it and fails
Changing code to see what happens
quiz.why: The test confirms the bug and then confirms the fix.

quiz.q: A test always passes, even with broken code. What's going on?
o: It's useless: it has to fail when the code is wrong
quiz.why: A test that never fails protects nothing.

quiz.q: What does `chrome-devtools-mcp` let Claude see?
o: The page's console, network and performance
quiz.why: It's the same thing you look at in DevTools.

quiz.q: What does `/code-review` do?
o: Looks for bugs in your diff, a PR or a branch
quiz.why: It reviews; approving and merging is still the team's call.

quiz.q: What does `/verify` do?
o: Builds, runs and watches the app to check the change
quiz.why: It checks real behavior, not just the tests.

student.lead: If you're learning, Claude Code is a teacher with endless patience, as long as you don't ask it to do everything for you.

steps.d: With `learning-output-style`, Claude lets you write the key parts of the code and explains the why.
Ask "why?" and ask for another example when something doesn't click. Copying without understanding leaves you nothing.
`/powerup` brings lessons with animated demos of Claude Code's features.
`/usage` shows how much you've used; if you're near the limit, `/clear` between tasks saves a lot.
Pick something small you can finish, start with `/init` and show it. A finished project teaches more than ten started ones.

quiz.q: What does `learning-output-style` do?
o: Asks you to write the key parts and explains the why
quiz.why: You learn by doing, not by watching.

quiz.q: If Claude solves everything for you…
o: You learn less: ask it to explain and write parts yourself
quiz.why: What you don't practice doesn't stick.

quiz.q: What does `/usage` show?
o: How much you've used and how much you have left
quiz.why: It helps you not run out halfway through the week.

quiz.q: What's a good first project?
o: Something small you can finish and show
Nothing until you know it all
quiz.why: Finishing gives you confidence and something to show.

quiz.q: You don't understand an answer. What do you do?
o: Ask for a simpler explanation or another example
quiz.why: Asking again is free and it's how you learn most.

quiz.q: What is `/powerup`?
o: Interactive feature lessons with animated demos
quiz.why: It comes with Claude Code.
